item.title: Iran gives US 7 conditions to restart talks, says ‘threats won't achieve results’
item.description: Iran has officially presented seven demands to Washington for resuming negotiations, emphasizing the need to conclude hostilities and unfreeze assets. Alongside this diplomatic approach, Iran is readying itself for potential US military actions, adapting its military strategy to prioritize naval capabilities. Efforts are underway to swiftly resolve the ongoing conflict.

item.description: Japan’s Shigenobu Murofushi and his son Koji Murofushi jointly lit the cauldron at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, bringing the torch relay to a memorable end. Both Shigenobu and Koji are former Asian Games champions in hammer throw. The duo climbed the stairs to the podium together before lighting the cauldron.

item.title: Atlanta man arrested after phone wipe; new ruling allows border searches
item.description: US border agents can now search traveler cellphones without reasonable suspicion or a warrant. A recent court ruling affirmed this broad authority at international borders. This decision follows an incident where a phone was wiped during an airport search. The ruling impacts traveler privacy and government access to electronic data. It highlights ongoing debates about digital device searches at the border.

item.title: H1-B visa price hike extension: How this will impact Indian engineers, technicians
item.description: President Donald Trump has decided to maintain H-1B visa restrictions for an additional twelve months, extending their duration until September 21, 2027. Alongside this, a $100,000 fee will be required for select foreign professionals entering the U.S. This measure poses significant challenges for Indian engineers and skilled workers looking to advance their careers in America and may lead employers to alter their international recruitment strategies.

item.title: Rod Stewart’s former LA estate sold in two deals totaling $86 million
item.description: A legendary estate in Holmby Hills, previously owned by Rod Stewart, has fetched an impressive $86 million. The sprawling six-acre property was split into two parcels, with television producer David Zander acquiring the main mansion for $57 million. Meanwhile, Nick Kaiser purchased a smaller parcel complete with a historic cabin for $29 million. This notable sale underscores the ongoing allure of grand historic properties.

item.title: Psychology says feeling uneasy when someone is too kind doesn’t mean you’re ungrateful
item.description: Receiving kindness can be an uncomfortable experience for many, invoking feelings of awkwardness. This unease can originate from various psychological factors and past experiences. Some view kindness as an obligation or believe they must earn affection. Likewise, receiving compliments can conflict with one's self-perception. Cultivating the ability to accept little gestures of care can significantly reduce this discomfort.

item.title: Meet Neha Thakur, 25, Himachal Pradesh’s first woman truck driver
item.description: It’s not easy to switch careers! But a young girl from Himachal Pradesh left her air hostess training to become a truck driver. Meet 25-year-old Neha Thakur who chose a career path few would have expected. After graduating, she worked briefly in the aviation sector and today, she spends her days behind the wheel of a 16-tonne truck, travelling across India. Neha belongs from Khudla village in Sarkaghat, Mandi district, Himachal Pradesh. She is widely known as Himachal Pradesh’s first woman truck driver. She covers her journeys in her own social-media videos and vlogs.

item.title: 'When she returns to movies': Salman Khan slams those trolling Katrina Kaif
item.description: Salman Khan took a stand against the harmful practice of body and age shaming that plagues the internet. In a show of vulnerability, he shed his shirt and makeup to confront his critics about their hurtful comments, especially towards those dealing with postpartum weight gain. Moreover, he expressed discontent over paparazzi taking inappropriate photos of female celebrities, voicing his disdain for online hate and personal invasions.

item.title: IIT-Bombay suicide: Parents refuse to take son's body; crime branch to probe case
item.description: The abetment of suicide case involving an IIT-Bombay student has been transferred to the crime branch. An FIR was registered after the student's parents alleged casteist slurs and harassment. The student was found dead in his hostel room on Friday. His parents refused to claim the body until accused persons were arrested. The investigation is ongoing, and IIT-Bombay will cooperate fully with authorities.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Yashasvi Solanki becomes first woman officer to serve as President’s ADC
item.description: Lieutenant Commander Yashasvi Solanki made history in May 2025 by becoming the first woman officer from India’s Army, Navy or Air Force to serve as Aide-de-Camp to the President. A Haryana native and former district-level badminton and volleyball player, Solanki joined the Indian Navy in 2012. Her journey from sports and naval service to Rashtrapati Bhavan highlights discipline, perseverance and the changing role of women in India’s armed forces.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: UPI MDR: Can Rs 6,000 be split into three Rs 2,000 payments? No daily cap
item.description: The NPCI framework and the FAQs issued with it do not stipulate that multiple payments relating to a single bill must be clubbed together. Such a restriction, if in place, could prevent businesses from breaking up larger payments into multiple transactions of Rs 2,000 or less.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: 18 years after the 2008 financial meltdown: How a crisis born in US reshaped India
item.description: The 2008 global financial crisis hit India through markets, capital flows and trade, but its banking system remained resilient. The shock exposed gaps in financial resolution and regulation, prompting reforms including the IBC, stronger safeguards for systemically important banks and higher buffers. Nearly 18 years later, India is stronger, but rising AI investment raises fresh questions about leverage and financial stability.

item.description: England beat Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the third T20I at Old Trafford in Manchester on Saturday to complete a 3-0 series sweep. The hosts chased down Sri Lanka's 125-run target with 62 balls to spare. The win also helped England move back to the top of the T20 world rankings, replacing India.

item.title: Invasive spotted lanternfly reaches Canada after spreading across 18 US states
item.description: Canada confirmed its first spotted lanternfly detection in Windsor, Ontario. Movement restrictions are now in place to prevent further spread of this invasive species. Surrounding areas are under surveillance to assess the infestation's extent. This pest poses significant risks to agriculture and forestry industries. Early detection and reporting are crucial for managing its impact.

Subsequent unique cabins, like a treehouse, also achieved substantial financial success. Broomfield's ventures have now earned over $2.1 million in total revenue. He continues to expand his cabin empire for his family's future.
